Job Posting: Environmental Scientist (Limited-Term)

Department of Parks & Recreation

JC-534918



Environmental Scientist (Limited-Term)
  
ENVIRONMENTAL SCIENTIST

$4,418.00 - $9,321.00 per Month
  
New to State candidates will be hired into the minimum salary of the classification or minimum of alternate range when applicable.

**Final Filing Date:** **11/2/2026**

**Application Methods:**

Electronic (Using your CalCareer Account)

By Mail

Drop-off

Print Job

Save Job

### **Job Description and Duties**

**ENVIRONMENTAL SCIENTIST (LIMITED-TERM) – ANGELES DISTRICT/ NATURAL RESOURCES/ MALIBU CREEK STATE PARK**

  

The Angeles District has an opening for an Environmental Scientist (LT). Under the direction of the Senior Environmental Scientist (Supervisory), serves as the coordinator for the Angeles District Natural Resources Volunteer Program. The incumbent coordinates, organizes, and oversees volunteer projects focused on habitat restoration, invasive plant removal, and community stewardship. This position provides guidance to ensure ecological goals and safety standards are met, while also building partnerships with community groups, schools, and nonprofits. The position is responsible for volunteer program reporting and contributes to the success of SMMC-funded wildfire recovery initiatives.
  
  
This position is a 12-month Limited-Term position that may be extended and/or become permanent.

The incumbent exercises a high degree of initiative, judgment, and analytical skill in coordinating sensitive and high-priority assignments that require collaboration with internal divisions, the Natural Resources Agency, control agencies, and other stakeholders.
  
  
This position is designated as not telework eligible.

  

Training and Development Assignments may be considered.

  

This position requires a valid Class C driver’s license. You must answer the questions addressing your driver’s license on your application. Ensure you provide your driver’s license number, class, expiration date, and any endorsements and/or restrictions on your application.

The selected candidate is required to submit to a background investigation process utilizing Live Scan fingerprinting prior to appointment.

**State housing is not available.** For further information contact Jacoub Mahshi at (424) 508-0465 or Jacoub.Mahshi@parks.ca.gov.

**This recruitment may be used to fill identical vacancies which may occur within 180 days of the Final Filing Date of this job posting.**

You will find additional information about the job in the **Duty Statement**.

### **Working Conditions**

Effective July 1, 2025, the California Department of Human Resources (CalHR) implemented the Personal Leave Program 2025 (PLP 2025). PLP 2025 directs that each employee receives a temporary reduction in pay in exchange for PLP 2025 leave credits. The percentage of the temporary salary reduction and the number of PLP 2025 leave credits are determined by the position’s assigned bargaining unit. **The salary range(s) included in this job advertisement do not reflect the temporary salary reduction.** For additional information regarding PLP 2025, please click here.  
  
  
  
  
Work environment is an office/outdoor setting, using computers, telephone and other business equipment. Typical work activities involve frequent and prolonged periods of sitting. Typical work involves extended telephone conversations and keyboard operation. Must meet many deadlines within short time frames. Hand dexterity to use telephone, keyboard and calculators are common requirements. Move about, stand, reach, stoop or bend. Use fine motor skills for computer or office machine use. Lift minimum weight of 25 pounds. Use of hand cart to move supplies over 10 pounds of weight. Requires reaching, twisting, turning, kneeling, bending, stooping, squatting, crouching, grasping and making repetitive hand movements in the performance of daily duties. May involve some exposure to aggressive visitors. Will work outdoors in unpredictable weather ranging from extreme heat to extreme cold. May be required to perform arduous field work in rugged, steep terrain. May encounter wild animals. Must be willing to work weekends, nights, and holidays as necessary. Travel maybe required to meetings, conferences, trainings, and on site project locations and may need to use personal vehicle if State Vehicles are not available.

  

### **Position Details**

**Job Code #:**

JC-534918

**Position #(s):**

549-915-0762-915

**Environmental Scientist (Limited-Term)**

**Classification:**

ENVIRONMENTAL SCIENTIST

$4,418.00 - $6,035.00 A

$5,370.00 - $7,350.00 B

$6,796.00 - $9,321.00 C

New to State candidates will be hired into the minimum salary of the classification or minimum of alternate range when applicable.

**# of Positions:**

1

Los Angeles County

In Office

12 Month Limited Term - Full Time

Angeles District

### **Department Information**

The mission of California State Parks is to provide for the health, inspiration, and education of the people of California by helping to preserve the state's extraordinary biological diversity, protecting its most valued natural and cultural resources, and creating opportunities for high-quality outdoor recreation.

All employees are responsible for contributing to an inclusive, safe, and secure work environment that values diverse cultures, perspectives, and experiences, and is free from discrimination.

Department Website: http://www.parks.ca.gov

* The position(s) require(s) a valid California Drivers License (CDL). You must answer the questions addressing your CDL on your application. Ensure you provide your CDL number, class, expiration date, and any endorsements and/or restrictions.
* The position(s) require(s) a Background Investigation be cleared prior to being hired.

jobs.description:
**Expression of Interest - Engineers | Technicians | Project Managers | Environmental Scientists**

**Bring your expertise. Build something meaningful in Bundaberg.**

Are you an experienced technical or project professional looking for an opportunity to combine meaningful project work with strong client relationships, business development and the potential to grow your leadership career?

GHD is seeking **Expressions of Interest** from experienced professionals interested in joining our **Bundaberg** team and leading our growth and presence across the Wide Bay region.

We’re deliberately keeping our search broad. Your project management or technical background could be in transport, civil, water, structural, electrical, environment or another technical discipline. What matters most is your ability to bring strong consulting experience, work closely with clients and contribute to both project delivery and business growth.

**Build your career, and a great life, in Bundaberg**  
If you’ve been thinking about swapping the pace of a major city for a regional lifestyle without stepping back from your career, Bundaberg offers the opportunity to do both.

With the coast on your doorstep, a relaxed regional lifestyle and easy access to destinations such as Bargara and the Southern Great Barrier Reef, Bundaberg offers a different way to build your career. Whether you’re already based in Queensland or considering a move from interstate, it’s an opportunity to enjoy the benefits of regional living while continuing to develop your career with a global professional services company.

**What could your opportunity look like?**  
Depending on your experience and background, you could join us as an **Engineer, Technician, Project Manager or Environmental Scientist** .

We’re particularly interested in people who enjoy combining hands-on project delivery with building trusted client relationships, identifying opportunities and growing the business.

You may already be an established senior professional, or you may be ready to broaden your influence, take on greater client and commercial responsibility and continue developing towards future leadership opportunities.

This opportunity isn’t defined by a single technical discipline. We’re looking for the right capability, consulting mindset and client orientation to complement our Bundaberg team and contribute to our continued growth across the region.

**What you’ll bring**

**We’d like to hear from you if you bring:**

* 5 plus years’ experience in consulting, technical delivery or project management
* A background in engineering, environment, project management or another relevant technical discipline
* Strong client-facing and relationship-building capability
* A commercial mindset and an interest in identifying and developing opportunities
* The ability and willingness to contribute directly to project delivery
* A collaborative approach and the ability to work across disciplines, projects and locations
* An interest in contributing to the continued growth of our Bundaberg business
* The ambition to continue developing your career and potentially move into broader leadership over time
* Relevant professional accreditation for your discipline, such as RPEQ and/or CPEng, or working towards attaining accreditation where applicable
  

You don’t need to already know the Queensland market. We’re interested in professionals who bring the right consulting and client-focused approach, valuable experience and a willingness to collaborate with colleagues who have strong local market knowledge.

**Why GHD?**  
At GHD, you’ll have the opportunity to combine your technical expertise, project experience and client relationships while being connected to a broader multidisciplinary business. This isn’t about fitting into a narrowly defined role. We’re interested in what you could bring to Bundaberg.

Whether you’re an experienced engineer, project manager, technical specialist or consultant looking for greater influence, broader client exposure and an opportunity to contribute to regional growth, we’d like to hear from you.

**Interested?** Register your interest and start a conversation with us about what your career with GHD in Bundaberg could look like. https://www.bundabergregion.org/
  
  
GHD is an equal opportunity employer, and we want everyone to be able to fully participate in our recruitment process. We value a diverse workforce and an inclusive culture. We encourage applications from Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples and people of all identities.

GHD embraces a range of flexible work practices to create a work environment focused on well-being, flexibility and productivity where our people can thrive.

We respectfully ask that no agency resumes be presented at this stage.
  
#LI-JW1

  

**Come together and make a meaningful impact.**

We bring our people together to create something bigger and solve some of the world's most complex problems. Come and experience the power of commitment and see strategy and ideas come to life when you join GHD.

**Let's drive real change.**

**Our Pledge to You**  
At GHD, we don’t just believe in the power of commitment, we live and breathe it every day.

That’s why we pledge to empower our people to make a positive impact. Combining our deep technical expertise with the capabilities of our clients and partners, we respond to some of the most complex challenges facing our planet today.

See where your commitment could take you.
  
That’s the **#PowerOfCommitment**

**Who we are**  
GHD is a global professional services company that leads through engineering, architecture, and construction expertise. We are an employee-owned company with over 11,000 diverse and skilled individuals, across more than 200 offices spanning five continents.

jobs.title: Senior Environmental Assessment and Approvals Specialist
jobs.description:
**Senior Environmental Assessment and Approvals Specialist**
============================================================

Location:
Perth Office - CBD, WA, AU

23 Oct 2026

**Senior Environmental Assessment and Approvals Specialist – Permanent and 12 month Secondment / Max Term Contract – Perth CBD**

  

We have two upcoming opportunities for Senior Assessment & Approvals Specialists to join our team on a Permanent and 12-month secondment / maximum term contract.

In this role, you will lead and support the development of strategic network plans and asset strategies. Your primary focus will be on clearly identifying SHE requirements associated with our work programs, influencing external stakeholders to secure strategic safety and environment statutory approvals and requirements for future growth, development and protection of the network.

**Your Role in Action**

* Identify key environmental, planning and/or heritage constraints to facilitate project design, scoping and successful delivery and assist Western Power in delivering outcomes by providing timely and relevant environmental advice (including technical/operational, approvals, strategy and risk).

* Supporting and mentoring the business to identify, assess, manage and acquit SHE requirements, including but not limited to environmental, pollution, land access, urban and regional planning and public safety requirements during the planning, development and prioritisation of the work program and associated projects in a timely manner.

* Influence the development of strategic network plans, asset strategies, network design standards and work programs that lead to improved SHE outcomes and reduction of associated risk to a level that is as low as reasonably practicable.

* Lead and support the development and implementation of SHE requirements that govern access to the network for the purpose of construction, maintenance and inspection and promote improved SHE outcomes.

* Develop and manage relationships with external planning and infrastructure stakeholders to ensure the appropriate placement of our network assets, in consideration of our objectives.

* Monitor and implement improvements to SHE requirements to ensure continuous improvement of as part of a closed loop feedback process.

* Provide Subject Matter Expertise and advice in relation to environment, heritage and urban and regional planning advice to the SHE or SP&A Function and broader business.

* Representing the SHE or SP&A Function at internal and external engagement and training sessions.

**What Makes You a Great Fit**

* Bachelor’s Degree in environmental science, science, urban and regional planning, law or related discipline

* Solid experience in environment, heritage and statutory planning approvals.

* Experience in Public and environmental safety matters and the development of risk reducing performance improvement strategies

* Excellent stakeholder management, communication and written skills

* Proven ability to influence key internal and external stakeholders in relation to SEQT outcomes

* Demonstrated experience with community engagement

* Demonstrated ability to work within a dynamic environment and to work autonomously

* A sound understanding of the regulations and arrangements associated with infrastructure planning, land development, environmental assessments, and heritage and land access.

* Experience managing environmental consultants is desirable, including consultant engagement, contract performance and financial management

By joining Western Power, you will contribute to powering a cleaner energy future. We are dedicated to fostering career development and promoting a healthy work-life balance, empowering you to drive innovation as we develop a network that will serve the Western Australian community for generations. You will also benefit from a range of perks and opportunities, including:

* Over 50% of our employment opportunities are driven by career progression.

* Flexible work arrangements to support part time work, working hours, working from home arrangements and job share.

* The opportunity to purchase up to four weeks of additional leave per year.

* Access to salary packaging, social club activities, and discounted health insurance and gym membership.

* An award-winning employee recognition and benefits programme.

* An innovative team culture that’s enabling the transition to renewable energy and decarbonisation.

* In addition to standard leave, enjoy three wellness leave days each year.

* Access to end-of-trip facilities at our Perth office and South Metro Depot, perfect for cyclists.

* On-site café available for convenient meals and refreshments throughout the day.

* 22 weeks paid parental leave and 5 days of First Nations cultural leave to support family and cultural connections.

**Applications close on 6 November 2026.**

We value diversity and inclusivity, encouraging applications from all backgrounds, including women, Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people, and LGBTQIA+ communities. As a WORK180-endorsed employer for women, we are proud of our commitment to inclusion. You can learn more about this through our Reconciliation Action Plan and Disability Access and Inclusion Plan.

Learn more about Western Power here: About (westernpower.com.au)

Find out how we’re building A Network for Life: A network for life (westernpower.com.au)
